title: Ex 10.12 · 9 divides 4^(3n) + 8
prompt: Prove by induction that $9 \mid (4^{3n} + 8)$ for every integer $n \ge 0$. Check $n = 0$, assume $4^{3k} + 8 = 9m$ for an integer $m$ (the case $n = k$), and show that $4^{3(k+1)} + 8$ is $9$ times an integer.
answer_format: A structured proof: a base step (the case n = 0 with numbers only), an assume step (f(k) = d·m for an integer m), expr steps for the n = k + 1 case, and a witness step (the integer w with f(k + 1) = d·w). Notes optional. No final answer box.
hints: Base case: for n = 0, 4⁰ + 8 = 1 + 8 = 9. (Remember 4⁰ is 1, not 0.)
4^(3(k + 1)) = 64·4^(3k). Rewrite 64·4^(3k) + 8 so that the block 4^(3k) + 8 appears.
solution: Inductive step: suppose $9 \mid (4^{3k} + 8)$ for some $k \ge 0$, so $4^{3k} + 8 = 9m$ for an integer $m$.
So $9 \mid (4^{3(k+1)} + 8)$, and by induction $9 \mid (4^{3n} + 8)$ for every integer $n \ge 0$. $\blacksquare$
